notable_absence.finding: The promoted eventing:function-scope concept states that a wildcard *.* scope requires Full Admin or Eventing Full Admin, while any other bucket/scope value only requires a role scoped to that bucket/scope. Nothing on this page states any role or privilege requirement at all for --deploy/--undeploy/--pause/--resume/--delete/--import/--export, wildcard or otherwise - the identical RBAC-citation gap already found on the analytics-link-setup page (file 1 of this batch), now confirmed a second time on a second, unrelated CLI subcommand. This looks like a batch-wide pattern in the couchbase-cli reference tree rather than a one-off omission on either page.

cross_component_finding: This page's own H1 title ('Manage Events') and DESCRIPTION ('...functions in the Event service') both use 'Event service' - singular, dropping the '-ing' - rather than 'Eventing Service', the name used by the promoted service:eventing-service concept and by every eventing: concept label in the registry (Eventing Function, Function Scope, Eventing Storage, etc.). This is exactly the CLI-vs-REST/UI terminology drift the round brief asked to watch for, and it appears on the very first Eventing CLI page checked in this batch - the tool's own generated reference does not use the product's own service name consistently.
cross_product_finding: eventing:deployment-feed-boundary is documented elsewhere (per the registry) with Title-Case UI labels ('Everything' / 'From Now'); this CLI page's own flag literals are lower-kebab-case ('from-everything' / 'from-now') - a third spelling register for the same two-valued setting, on top of the UI-label case difference already implicit in the registry note. The --boundary flag itself is marked '(Deprecated)' on this CLI page with no replacement flag and no version given, while nothing in the registry's own eventing:deployment-feed-boundary entry mentions a deprecation - suggesting the boundary-at-deploy-time mechanism may be deprecated specifically on this CLI surface (superseded by boundary-at-function-definition-time, most likely) while remaining current on the REST/UI surface the registry concept was drawn from. This is a candidate for a docs-issue: a deprecated CLI flag with no stated replacement or removal version.
